title: Orsen and the Inheritance
premise: Retired detective Juniper Villalobos receives a confession letter for the cold-case drowning of Orsen Halloran, postmarked the day after the sender's funeral, claiming the death was no accident and pointing to a hidden inheritance. Reopening the case drags Juniper back into the orbit of the found family that once saved them, including Orsen's daughter Marisol, who believes her father's death was settled truth. As the statute of limitations closes in, Juniper uncovers that three people conspired to protect a survivor of abuse, and that the confession was written by the one person who never stopped loving Orsen. In the end, Juniper must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile family that built their bookshop life, closing the case by finally telling it whole.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent fifteen years filing the paperwork of other people's tragedies. They write mysteries about quiet people who keep dangerous secrets out of love.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A week after burying their old friend Delia, Juniper finds a confession letter among condolence cards: Delia admits she witnessed Orsen Halloran's drowning twenty-two years ago and it was not an accident. The emotional beat is dread wrapped in grief, as Juniper realizes the letter names them as the only person Delia trusted to finish what she couldn't.

chapters.title: The Case That Wasn't Cold
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Digging through the official file, Juniper finds the drowning ruled accidental within forty-eight hours and notices Delia's name redacted from witness lists. Marisol Halloran visits the bookshop, suspicious of why Juniper is asking questions. The beat is unease: every answer opens two more questions.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A lawyer friend confirms any charges expire in nineteen days, but civil claims against an estate do not, hinting at the hidden inheritance. Juniper maps the old lakeside community and realizes all surviving witnesses still live within ten miles of each other. The beat is mounting pressure and the first taste of obsession returning.

chapters.title: Marisol's Version
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She recounts her childhood: her father's kindness, his secret meetings with a frightened teenager named Wren, and the night he never came home. She warns Juniper that reopening the wound will destroy people she loves. The beat is tenderness laced with threat; love and duty begin to pull apart.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Tracking down Wren, now living under another name, Juniper discovers the teenager Orsen was protecting was being abused by a powerful local benefactor, Aldous Crane. Wren refuses to speak and begs Juniper to let the dead rest. The beat is heartbreak: survival has cost Wren everything, including the truth.

chapters.title: What Delia Saw
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Among Delia's effects, Juniper finds her diary: she saw three figures at the lake that night, not one, and one of them was someone she loved. Meanwhile Crane's lawyer serves Juniper with a cease-and-desist. The beat is betrayal and escalation; the mystery turns inward toward Juniper's own circle.

chapters.title: The Third Figure
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts her mother, Ruth, who confesses she was on the dock that night, that Orsen died accidentally while shielding Wren from Crane, and that she and Delia buried the truth to protect Wren and the family from Crane's retaliation. The beat is devastating relief: the accident was real, but the silence was a choice.

chapters.title: Crane's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper learns Orsen's 'hidden inheritance' was evidence, a documented ledger of Crane's abuses meant to free Wren, which Ruth hid to keep everyone safe. With days left, Juniper retrieves it from the lake boathouse as Crane's men close in. The beat is thriller-pace urgency and moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Confrontation at the bookshop: Crane demands the ledger, Wren arrives ready to testify at last, and Juniper must decide whether justice served now is worth shattering the family that survived by staying silent. The beat is the climax, love against duty with everything on the table.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Crane is exposed when Wren testifies and the ledger goes public; Orsen is reburied with his true story told. Marisol forgives her mother, Wren begins to heal, and Juniper shelves the case file beside Delia's letter, finally at peace. The beat is bittersweet resolution: some families are found twice, once in life and once in truth.
